messages:
sasha: Heads-up — running long-context replay job and seeing persistent memory growth. Heap climbs ~35-45MB/min under heavy longctx (8k tokens). KV cache pages keep increasing even after steady state. Suspect cross-request key variability + prefix churn -> fragmentation. Attaching quick profiler snapshot below.

jeff: Can you paste the profiler output and an example cache key? Which model and batch config?

sasha: model=redwood-xl-3b, batch=8, seq=8192. Example keys look like: `usr:acct:prompt_v2:phash:nonce123456` — the trailing nonce is per-request. Profiler excerpt: 
```
KV stats: total_pages=1_200_432
unique_prefixes=123_412
avg_page_fill=0.48
fragmentation_est=0.23
heap_growth_rate=38MB/min
active_sessions=1_400

longctx_evictions/sec=0.12
prefix_collision_count=3_200
```

maria: that nonce is the problem — it's intentionally added at prompt gen time to dedupe request ids, but we're using the entire prompt id in the cache key. That guarantees low reuse.

alex: Agreed. Two orthogonal ideas: (1) canonicalize prefix shapes by dropping request nonce before hashing for KV key derivation, (2) add a small affinity token for session-stickiness so multi-turn still benefits. Also we should avoid losing tenant/role info.

jeff: privacy/PII check: dropping nonce is fine, it doesn't contain PII. But confirm no per-request secret is being removed. For cross-tenant isolation we keep tenant_id/region in the key.

sasha: Quick local experiment: patched keying in runtime to strip last nonce segment when prefixing. Results on replay harness for same trace:
```
before: cache_hit_rate=7%  mem_growth=38MB/min  pages=1_200_432
after:  cache_hit_rate=62% mem_growth=6MB/min   pages=470_211
```
Quality check: end-to-end outputs identical for canonical prompts, ~0.3% diffs for traces that relied on nonce as part of prompt (rare).

maria: That's promising. Need to ensure function-calling and structured output flows that rely on exact keying aren't broken. We should add an opt-in flag behind config so Dedicated/private customers can enable by policy.

alex: Also saw micro-issue: when canonicalized keys collide across short-lived sessions we temporarily saw hot-page thrash because multiple sessions now map to same page. Mitigation: add lightweight per-session affinity token (small stable id appended to page shard) that preserves per-session locality without including full nonce.

jeff: Proposed rollout: 1) upstream key canonicalizer patch (strip-nonce + optional session-affinity token), 2) add telemetry: prefix_hit_rate, page_fill_by_prefix_shape, fragmentation_metric, and longctx_mem_growth. 3) canary on staging + 48h perf/regression checks, 4) enable on Hosted gradually, default off for Dedicated/Private (config toggle).

sasha: I'll open a PR with the patch + perf harness results and a canary plan. Short checklist: include migration-note (keys change -> cache cold start), add flag `runtime.kv.strip_nonce_in_prefix` (false by default), add `runtime.kv.session_affinity` (false by default).

maria: Also add an eval that runs a set of prompts that are sensitive to exact prefix hashes so we can detect correctness regressions automatically. Put a threshold for allowed output drift (e.g., ROUGE/BLEU-based or embedding similarity).

kv-bot: deploy-bot: canary created -> env=staging, build=kv-keyshape-canonicalizer-20260308, canary_id=canary-1192 :rocket:

jeff: Good. After canary, if prefix_hit_rate increases and mem_growth falls to <10MB/min and no quality regressions, schedule gradual rollout. If we see fragmentation spike, revert and iterate on session_affinity params.

sasha: Thanks — PR + perf artifacts incoming in ~2h. If anyone wants to pair on the diagnostic traces, ping me. :mag:
